# Global convex-potential approximation of contact actions

This note proves an exact limitation of the paired-support addition
construction. Every fixed finite response vector of its actions is
approximated by actual erosions from ONE nonnegative convex potential
independent of the continuous normal. Therefore it gives no stronger
strict finite-response alternative than the archived all-convex-potential
dual. Exact addition still has constructive value for prescribed speeds
and exact equalities; the approximation does not preserve neutral
responses at any finite penalty parameter.

The final disk example proves that last warning for the newly defined
physical retained-cap response. It does not prove that the two exact
finite-response classes differ.

## 1. Actual family and action

Let P be a finite complete integer base, with positive convex fibers
K_z in R^d, d>=1, satisfying every anchored Minkowski inclusion. Let

 C=conv(union_(z in P) {z} times K_z),   Q=conv(P).

Work in aff(P) times R^d if the base rank is deficient. All surface
integrals below are on the finitely many actual measured fiber
boundaries, with measure eta=sum_z H_(d-1)|_(boundary K_z). In d=1
this means counting measure on the two endpoints of each interval.

An action is the actual intersection of C with cuts

 u.x+e V_i(u,z,x)<=ell_i(u,z),   u in S^(d-1), i in I,           (1)

where I is finite, ell_i is affine in z and continuous in u,
ell_i(u,z)>=h_(K_z)(u) on every original base, and V_i is finite,
nonnegative, continuous and convex in (z,x). All fields are defined
on one common open convex neighborhood of C. Globally finite fields
are a special case. The action may already be the Cartesian-product
sum of several earlier actions.

At a regular boundary point x of K_z, write n=n_z(x). The proved
radial formula gives the exact inward physical speed

 v(z,x)=max({V_i(n,z,x):ell_i(n,z)=h_(K_z)(n)} union {0}).        (2)

No contact is required if this maximum is zero. Nonregular points
have eta-measure zero and do not affect any response below.

For every (z,x) in the FULL original C, the affine gaps

             g_i(u,z,x)=ell_i(u,z)-u.x                           (3)

are nonnegative. Indeed this holds on every generating fiber, and
affineness in both physical variables extends it to their convex hull.
This whole-body fact is essential to the uniform domination below.

## 2. One global penalty potential and its boundary limit

For a finite penalty L>=0 define

 Phi_L(z,x)=max_(i in I, u in S^(d-1))
                     [V_i(u,z,x)-L g_i(u,z,x)]_+.              (4)

The maximum is over a compact parameter set and is attained. It is
finite and continuous: locally uniform continuity of the displayed
family on compact physical sets proves continuity of its maximum.
It is nonnegative and convex in the full physical variables, because
each V_i-Lg_i is convex and positive parts and suprema preserve
convexity. If I is empty, use the zero potential and zero action.

If the fields were only given on a neighborhood, (4) can be extended
to a globally finite nonnegative convex function without changing it
on C. Choose a small compact convex thickening C_delta inside that
neighborhood. The subgradients of the finite convex Phi_L are bounded
on C_delta by local Lipschitz continuity. The supremum of its supporting
affine functions based at points of C_delta, together with zero, is
therefore globally finite and convex, agrees with Phi_L on C_delta,
and is nonnegative. This is done for each FIXED L; no uniform global
Lipschitz constant in L is asserted. In a deficient base span extend
constantly in its orthogonal complement. This changes no lattice or
measured point.

Let B=max_(i,u,(z,x) in C)V_i(u,z,x)<infinity. By (3), on C one has

                0<=Phi_L<=B,   Phi_(L')<=Phi_L for L'>=L.      (5)

At every regular measured boundary point,

                         Phi_L(z,x) decreases to v(z,x).       (6)

Here is the exact compactness proof. If g_i(u,z,x)=0, then

 ell_i(u,z)>=h_(K_z)(u)>=u.x

forces equality throughout; thus u supports K_z at x. At a regular
point this means u=n_z(x). Conversely every index in (2) has zero gap
at this normal. Hence the maximum over zero-gap pairs is precisely v.
Each such pair is unchanged by the penalty, so Phi_L>=v.

For the reverse bound, if the limit of Phi_L is positive, choose a
maximizing pair (i_L,u_L) along an increasing sequence L->infinity.
Its nonnegative gap obeys L g_(i_L)<=V_(i_L)<=B, so the gap tends to
zero. Pass to a subsequence with fixed i and u_L->u. Continuity gives
g_i(u,z,x)=0 and limsup Phi_L<=V_i(u,z,x)<=v. If the limit is zero,
the inequality Phi_L>=v already proves (6). This includes the case
of no old contact and uses no regularity of the contact set.

Since eta is finite, (5)--(6) imply

               integral |Phi_L-v| d eta ->0.                   (7)

Thus every bounded measurable boundary test w satisfies

               integral w Phi_L d eta -> integral w v d eta.  (8)

In particular all fixed closed-cap inward selectors are allowed,
including their proper, inside-supporting, outside-supporting and
pure-integer statuses. Moreover convergence is uniform over any
uniformly bounded family of tests, since its error is bounded by
sup||w||_infinity times (7). This includes all continuous hinge weights
[1+u.(x-y)]_+ with u in a fixed compact optimizer set and finitely many
fixed marked points.

## 3. Actual old-roof erosion for fixed L

For real z in Q let h(z,u)=h_(C_z)(u), the support of the ACTUAL section
of the canonical hull. Equivalently,

 h(z,u)=max{sum_p alpha_p h_(K_p)(u):alpha_p>=0,
                          sum alpha_p=1, sum alpha_p p=z}.      (9)

The finite representation follows by grouping any convex representation
of a point of C by its base. It proves concavity in z; the support is
upper semicontinuous by compactness of C. The finite polyhedral roof
also gives continuity, though upper semicontinuity is enough for the
closed cuts below. At an original base it equals the given fiber
support by actual compatibility.

Fix L, and define the old normal-roof body

 C_(e,L)=C intersect intersection_(u in S^(d-1))
       { (z,x):u.x+e Phi_L(z,x)<=h(z,u)}.                       (10)

It is compact and convex: u.x+e Phi_L-h(z,u) is convex on Q times
R^d, and each inequality defines a closed set (h is upper
semicontinuous). It is nested as e grows. On each integer fiber,
Phi_L<=B on the original body, so a homothety about a fixed inner
ball center with fractional loss eB/r_z is contained in the new fiber.
For small e all original fibers remain positive. The projection is
still Q and no new or lost integer base occurs. These are actual
compatible bodies, not a family of separately assigned speeds.

For this fixed L, the radial first-variation proof applies on each
fiber to (10). At a regular point the old supporting normal is unique
and the same continuous field Phi_L occurs in every cut, so the
physical speed is exactly Phi_L(z,x). Thus, for every fixed finite
cap menu H_1,...,H_m,

 M-M_(e,L)=e D_L+o_L(e),
 mu(H_j)-mu_(e,L)(H_j)=e C_(j,L)+o_L(e),
 D_L=integral Phi_L d eta,
 C_(j,L)=integral kappa_j Phi_L d eta.                          (11)

The subscript on o_L is intentional: no estimate uniform in L is
needed or asserted. For the same reason, the physical retained-mass
derivative theorem applies for each fixed L. Equation (8) makes its
hinge responses converge uniformly over the old compact optimizer set;
therefore their attained minima converge as well, for any FIXED
prescribed mark velocity. This includes the centroid's nonunique
hinge set and the normalized secondary response.

## 4. Exact limit order and the response-cone limitation

Let R_j=C_j-beta D be any finite list of signed fixed-cap responses
of the original action. Equation (8) gives R_(j,L)->R_j. If every
R_j>0, choose ONE finite L so large that every R_(j,L)>0. Only after
that choice, take e>0 small enough that all expansions (11) preserve
their strict signs. The old-roof potential then gives the same kind
of strict finite-response improvement. No simultaneous L(e)->infinity
limit or uniform little-o estimate has been used.

The same statement holds for any finite list of fixed bounded signed
boundary tests, including specified hinge rows. For a compact optimal-
hinge family one uses the uniform estimate following (8). A strict
physical-T secondary inequality with fixed mark velocity transfers;
an exact equality or a nonstrict feasibility constraint does not
automatically transfer.

Conversely, every old nonnegative continuous convex potential Phi is
already realizable at the measured fibers by a finite action: take
one continuous global support ell_p(u,z) touching each base p and put
the SAME field Phi on all of these supports. Such bounded continuous
support selections exist by the archived finite Farkas/KKT theorem.
At each base z the p=z support is active in every normal, and all
fields have the same value. Its physical speed is therefore Phi on
every regular measured boundary point. In fact its integer fibers
coincide exactly with the old-roof fibers, since
min_p ell_p(u,z)=h_(K_z)(u) at every original base z.

It follows that, for any fixed finite list of linear response
coordinates, the closures of the old nonnegative convex-potential
response cone and the finite contact-action response cone are equal.
Their polar dual inequalities are identical. In particular a signed
stress that pairs nonpositively with EVERY old convex potential also
pairs nonpositively with every new contact action, by (8). Adding
separate signed affine equalities to an older dual cannot invalidate
this implication. The paired-support operation supplies exact
constructive addition, but no stronger strict all-potentials dual.

This closure statement alone does not prove that the exact finite
response sets coincide. It also does not preserve exact primary
neutrality, exact secondary ties, or a specified active incidence
pattern at finite L. Those remain separate from strict improvement.

## 5. Exact disk warning for neutral physical-T response

Let d=2,n=0, K be the closed unit disk, and fix 0<a<1. Consider the
actual action

          u.x+e(1+a u_1)<=1 for every unit u.                  (12)

Its body is the disk of radius 1-e centered at -e a e_1. It is nested
in K since a<1. Its boundary speed is v(n)=1+a n_1. The prescribed
mark y_e=-e a e_1 is its EXACT ordinary centroid and deepest point.
In particular T_(K_e)(y_e)/|K_e|=1 for every small e; its normalized
physical-T response is exactly neutral.

Here the global penalty potential (4) is explicit:

                    Phi_L(x)=[1-L+|Lx+a e_1|]_+.              (13)

On the unit circle it is strictly positive for every finite L>=0:
its minimum is 1-L+|L-a|>=1-a. Write c=n_1 and let

 delta_L(c)=Phi_L(n)-v(n)
          =sqrt(L^2+2La c+a^2)-L-a c>=0.                        (14)

For 0<c<1,

 delta_L(c)-delta_L(-c)
   =2ac{2L/[sqrt(L^2+2La c+a^2)
                    +sqrt(L^2-2La c+a^2)]-1}<0.              (15)

Indeed the denominator is strictly greater than 2L by the strict
triangle inequality for the two vectors with nonzero transverse
components. This also holds at L=0 directly. Reflection across the
vertical axis and integration therefore give

 integral_(circle) n_1 delta_L(n_1)dS<0,
 integral_(circle) n_2 delta_L(n_1)dS=0.                         (16)

The old first moment is B=integral n v(n)dS=pi a e_1. The penalty
speed has B_L=integral n Phi_L(n)dS, and (16) says B_L!=B for EVERY
finite L, although B_L->B by (7).

Keep the original mark velocity w=-a e_1 in the actual old-roof body
(10). The exact centroid formula in the physical-T variation source,
using that the unit-disk gauge is Euclidean norm and V=pi, gives

 d/de|_(0+) [T_(K_(e,L))(-e a e_1)/|K_(e,L)|]
                  =-|B_L-pi a e_1|/pi<0.                     (17)

Thus the finite penalty approximation destroys this prescribed exact
neutral secondary response, approaching it from the negative side.
Following the NEW centroid velocity would remove the penalty, but
that changes the prescribed mark motion and may change other response
constraints. Such a repair cannot be silently assumed.

For precision, this example is NOT an exact-class separation. The
global convex potential [1+a x_1]_+ has the original boundary trace
v(n) exactly. It shows that the particular monotone penalty approximation
does not preserve equality at finite L, not that no other potential
could preserve it. No universal exact-response equality is claimed.

## 6. What exact addition still retains

The paired-support construction combines finitely many chosen actions
with exactly the sum of their physical speeds. Therefore it preserves
all exact linear response identities those sums satisfy, before any
limit is taken. This is useful for constructing or checking a
prescribed neutral deformation. The penalty approximation proves only
closure of the old potential response set and cannot substitute for
that exact identity when feasibility requires an equality.

At the level of all boundary traces, exact realization by one continuous
potential need not hold. For example on the disk choose a closed proper
arc A with nonempty interior and define ell(u)=1+dist(u,A)^2, V(u)=1.
This is a legitimate continuous global-support action. Its speed is one
on A and zero on the complementary open arc, up to the two endpoint
normals. No continuous potential on K has that trace almost everywhere:
continuity forces the constants one and zero on the respective open
arcs and then contradicts continuity at their endpoints. The penalty
potentials nevertheless converge in surface L1 as proved above.

This boundary-trace example also does not prove separation by finitely
many response coordinates. Without an additional exact feasibility or
closedness theorem, the surviving advantage is constructive exact
control, not a stronger strict separating-dual theorem or an OC payment.
